  "consensus_summary": "The primary meaning is God and especially Jesus Christ as the Sun of Righteousness (divine glory, light, righteousness, healing presence), anchored in Malachi 4:2, Psalm 84:11, Transfiguration, and Revelation glory texts. Common alternatives include rulers/authorities (Gen 37), darkening as judgment, the righteous shining like the sun, and related polyvalent uses; consensus treats the christological/divine sense as the settled default while acknowledging context-dependence.",
  "book_summary": "The sun is the Father, the source of light from which every lesser light is drawn; the righteous shall shine as the sun in His kingdom.",
  "consensus_core_identification": "God/Christ (divine glory, righteousness, and light-giving presence)",
  "book_core_identification": "The Father (source of light); the righteous shining as the sun",
  "core_relation": "BOOK_NARROWS",
  "extension_relation": "PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION",
  "boundary_disagreement": "Book narrows the divine referent from the consensus default of God-and-especially-Christ to specifically the Father as hierarchical source, elevates the righteous-shining motif (a consensus alternative) into the core entry itself, and deploys Gen 37:9 in support of a fatherly reading while omitting the Malachi Christological texts and judgment/darkening cases that consensus treats as common.",
  "material_contradiction": "None; Father falls inside the consensus category of God, and the righteous-shining reading is already attested as an alternative, so the claims can coexist under polyvalence even though primacy and precision differ.",
  "rationale": "Minimum cores both center on the divine as light (Ps 84:11) plus the Matt 13:43 shining of the righteous, so the general referent category is preserved rather than replaced. The book nevertheless materially refines by restricting the divine person to the Father, adding the 'source of every lesser light' hierarchy, and folding the righteous comparison into the primary statement; this alters extension and boundary (excluding or demoting the dominant Christological cases) without producing a logical contradiction that would force rejection of the consensus core. Hence REFINED rather than MATCH, DIVERGENT, or NOVEL.",
  "citation_support": "PARTIAL",
  "strongest_objection": "Consensus primary rests on Malachi 4:2 and NT Christ-glory texts that the book's entry and printed citations entirely omit, so the shift to 'the Father' may be viewed as an idiosyncratic demotion of the traditional Sun-of-Righteousness identification.",
  "confidence": "high"
